standard.title: Test and refine design ideas
standard.description: generate, test, iterate and communicate design ideas, processes and solutions using technical terms and graphical representation techniques, including using digital tools
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can generate, iterate and communicate design ideas, decisions and processes using technical terms and graphical representation techniques, including using digital tools (AC9TDE6P02). They have generated and communicated ideas but have not yet systematically tested ideas through prototyping, used multiple generation strategies, or produced formal production drawings with scale and symbols.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students generate design ideas using multiple strategies, test ideas through models and prototypes, iterate based on testing, and communicate ideas and processes using annotated concept sketches, production drawings with technical terms, scale and symbols, and digital tools.

nodes.label: Generating ideas with multiple strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a variety of strategies to generate design ideas rather than committing to a first idea
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one strategy (e.g. brainstorming, sketching, experimenting) to generate multiple design ideas; communicate each idea clearly enough for feedback
nodes.typical_width: Use multiple strategies (brainstorming, sketching, 3D modelling, experimenting) to generate innovative ideas; investigate benefits and drawbacks of ideas including factors that may help or hinder the project
wider: Use digital polling or community consultation to capture diverse views and inform which ideas to develop further
Limited width — idea generation strategies are a finite set. The breadth comes from the variety of design challenges they are applied to.
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who only sketch produce variants of the same idea — without multiple generation strategies they arrive at Node 2 with a single design direction that cannot be meaningfully tested against alternatives, and at Node 3 with nothing substantive to communicate as a design process.
success_criteria: Generates more than one design idea for the same brief
Communicates each idea clearly enough for someone else to give feedback

response_modes.reason: Idea generation requires a repertoire of strategies before students can select the right one for a design challenge. Students who only sketch will produce variants of the same idea. Building familiarity with multiple generation strategies (brainstorming, sketching, experimenting, 3D modelling) is the prior condition for genuine alternative generation.

nodes.label: Testing through models and prototypes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop models, prototypes or samples to test the functionality of design ideas before committing to production
nodes.minimum_width: Build a simple model or prototype of a design idea; test it for at least one functional requirement; record the result
nodes.typical_width: Develop models or prototypes using a range of materials and tools (including rapid prototyping tools like 3D printers); test functionality against design criteria; explain what the test revealed
wider: Develop prototypes at different fidelity levels — low-fidelity (cardboard, paper) vs high-fidelity (3D printed, digital) — and explain when each is appropriate in the design process
Test a prototype with potential users and incorporate their feedback into the iteration
success_criteria: Builds a model or prototype of a design idea
Tests it for at least one functional requirement and records the result

response_modes.reason: Students who skip testing and jump from idea to final production make design decisions based on assumption rather than evidence. Testing through prototyping builds the habit of evidence-based iteration. Seeing how different prototyping approaches (low vs high fidelity, different materials) reveal different kinds of information helps students understand that testing is a deliberate design strategy, not just a formality.

nodes.label: Communicating with technical drawings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can communicate design ideas and processes using annotated concept sketches and production drawings with technical terms, scale and symbols
nodes.minimum_width: Produce an annotated sketch of a design idea using at least two technical conventions (e.g. labels, dimensions, scale indication)
nodes.typical_width: Produce annotated concept sketches and production drawings using technical terms, scale, symbols, pictorial and aerial views; document the design process for an intended audience (e.g. digital portfolio)
wider: Create a digital portfolio that communicates each step of the design process to a specific audience, explaining how the idea evolved through testing and iteration
Produce perspective, orthogonal or pattern drawings appropriate to the product type
success_criteria: Produces a sketch with at least two technical conventions applied correctly
Someone unfamiliar with the design can understand the idea from the drawing

response_modes.reason: Technical drawing conventions (scale, symbols, annotation standards) require practice to apply consistently and accurately. The conventions don't vary across contexts — what varies is the product being drawn. Students need repeated practice producing technical drawings to build fluency.
